statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-42013 (GNUTLS-SA-2026-04-29-8): hostname verification of a certificate with an oversized Subject Alternative Name fell back to checking the DNS hostname against the Common Name (lib/x509/hostname-verify.c), and email verification likewise fell back to the email address in the subject DN (lib/x509/email-verify.c). The GnuTLS NEWS file and Alpine's APKBUILD give the advisory id as GNUTLS-SA-2026-04-27-8. GnuTLS fixed it in 3.8.13 with commit 29801bef00ecc0f23c0bac4cd333b269cd2c1af4: https://gitlab.com/gnutls/gnutls/-/commit/29801bef00ecc0f23c0bac4cd333b269cd2c1af4, https://gnutls.org/security-new.html, https://gitlab.com/gnutls/gnutls/-/blob/3.8.14/NEWS . Alpine's 3.23-stable gnutls APKBUILD builds gnutls from the upstream release and lists CVE-2026-42013 under its 3.8.13-r0 security fixes: https://gitlab.alpinelinux.org/alpine/aports/-/blob/3.23-stable/main/gnutls/APKBUILD . We downloaded every package built from the gnutls source in the Alpine 3.23 index of the DHI Alpine repository: gnutls, gnutls-c++, gnutls-dbg, gnutls-dev, gnutls-doc and gnutls-utils, each at 3.8.11-r0, 3.8.12-r0, 3.8.13-r0 and 3.8.14-r0 for x86_64 and aarch64, 48 apks, and checked each download against its index checksum; no gnutls package is published in the DHI Alpine security repository. The library code is in libgnutls.so.30 in the gnutls package; gnutls-c++ ships the C++ wrapper libgnutlsxx.so.30, the seven gnutls-utils programs list libgnutls.so.30 as a needed library, gnutls-dev ships headers, pkg-config data and the libgnutls.so and libgnutlsxx.so symbolic links and no static library, and gnutls-dbg ships debug symbols. The GnuTLS version string in libgnutls.so.30 reads 3.8.11, 3.8.12, 3.8.13 and 3.8.14 in the matching builds on both architectures. So 3.8.11-r0 and 3.8.12-r0 are affected and 3.8.13-r0 is the first fixed build; 3.8.14-r0 also carries the fix.

CVE-2026-42013: an oversized Subject Alternative Name made GnuTLS certificate validation fall back to checking the Common Name, which could let a remote attacker bypass proper hostname validation. Upstream advisory GNUTLS-SA-2026-04-29-8 (https://www.gnutls.org/security-new.html#GNUTLS-SA-2026-04-29-8, https://gitlab.com/gnutls/gnutls/-/issues/1849) was fixed in GnuTLS 3.8.13 by https://gitlab.com/gnutls/gnutls/-/commit/29801bef00ecc0f23c0bac4cd333b269cd2c1af4. Debian fixed it for trixie in gnutls28 3.8.9-3+deb13u4 (DSA-6281-1, https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-42013), which applies the 3.8.13 security patch set to 3.8.9. The only build of this owner currently published for Debian 13 is made from that Debian version; the changelog shipped in its libgnutls30t64 package on amd64 and arm64 records this CVE, and its libgnutls.so.30 library on both architectures contains the debug messages the fix adds ("oversized SAN ignored, disabling CN fallback" and "oversized SAN ignored, disabling DN fallback"). The range ends at that build, the lowest published version carrying the fix. Builds made from Debian's earlier 3.8.9-3+deb13u2 and 3.8.9-3+deb13u3 sources sort below it and are reported as affected.
